rv.q: Work in this gentre have been upping the ante on troubled relationship between awkward progenitors and progeny.
Overall, Elf left this Grinch-inclined critic with expectations pleasantly confounded, and full of seasonal good cheer.
There's an infectious enjoyment to the proceedings.
Efficient, slick, even cynical: Elf is all these.

But there is staunch support from Joe McGann, who bears an astonishing resemblance to Harold Evans, as the waspish Walter. The score boasts one really good song, in which a group of department-store Santas bemoan the smartness ofmodem kids. Otherwise, this is a show that doesn't so much invoke the spirit ofChristmas as market it.
The relentless predictability and lack of theatrical imagination left me frustrated.
